title: 1997 Constitution
text: The Gambia is governed under the 1997 Constitution of the Republic of The Gambia, which establishes it as a sovereign republic and sets out the structure of government, fundamental rights, and the rule of law.

title: Three Branches of Government
text: The Gambia's government is divided into three branches: the Executive (headed by the President), the Legislature (the National Assembly), and the Judiciary (the courts), each with separate powers to provide checks and balances.

title: The Executive
text: Executive power is vested in the President, who is both Head of State and Head of Government, elected directly by universal adult suffrage for a five-year term, and who appoints Cabinet ministers to run government ministries.

title: The National Assembly
text: The National Assembly is The Gambia's legislature, responsible for making laws, approving the national budget, and providing oversight of the executive branch. Members are elected from constituencies across the country.

title: The Judiciary
text: The judiciary is the independent branch responsible for interpreting the law and administering justice, headed by the Chief Justice, with a court system including the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, and High Court.

title: Bill of Rights
text: Chapter IV of the 1997 Constitution is the Bill of Rights, guaranteeing fundamental rights and freedoms including the right to life, personal liberty, freedom of expression, freedom of assembly, and freedom from discrimination.

title: Citizenship
text: Gambian citizenship can be acquired by birth, descent, registration, or naturalization, as set out in Chapter III of the Constitution, and citizens have both rights and civic duties under the law.

title: Civic Duties
text: Civic duties commonly emphasized in Gambian civic education include obeying the law, paying taxes, voting in elections, respecting the rights of others, and participating responsibly in community and national life.

title: Local Government Structure
text: The Gambia is divided into local government areas, including Banjul and Kanifing municipalities and several administrative regions, each with local councils responsible for local governance and service delivery.

title: Elections and the IEC
text: The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) is responsible for organizing and supervising presidential, National Assembly, and local government elections in The Gambia, and for maintaining the voter register.

title: Rule of Law
text: The rule of law means that all persons, institutions, and the government itself are accountable to laws that are publicly known, equally enforced, and consistent with human rights — a core principle underlying the Constitution.

title: Separation of Powers
text: Separation of powers is the principle of dividing government responsibilities into distinct branches so that no single branch has too much power, with each branch able to check the others' actions.
